OpenAI’s Governance team helps shape how the company responsibly develops and deploys increasingly capable AI. We bring together technical evidence, policy, and operational perspectives to help the company address emerging risks, resolve difficult questions, and make well-supported decisions.
Our work includes shaping and improving governance practices, supporting effective oversight, developing clear assessments and recommendations, and ensuring that decisions lead to action. We work closely with research, safety, security, legal, and product teams to identify gaps, reconcile different views, and improve our approach as capabilities and circumstances change.

We are looking for a curious, high-agency Research Program Manager who can reason from first principles, make sense of incomplete or conflicting information, and move difficult work forward. You will help shape the substance of governance reviews, connect ideas and evidence across teams, and develop recommendations that are both well-founded and practical.
The work requires someone who can use established approaches where they fit, recognize when circumstances call for a different approach, and update their thinking as new evidence emerges. You should bring sound judgment, a willingness to experiment and learn, and the program-management discipline to turn good analysis into action.
Depending on your experience and the team’s needs, your work may focus on safety advisory and board-level oversight, deployment governance, or standards and strategic partner commitments.

Bring together technical, policy, and operational inputs to develop coherent assessments, recommendations, and decision materials for governance bodies and senior leaders.
Work through emerging or ambiguous questions, test assumptions, identify gaps or conflicting evidence, and help determine what additional analysis or decisions are needed.
Engage critically with research, evaluations, safeguards, and risk assessments, working with the relevant experts to understand what the evidence supports and where uncertainty remains.
Partner with governance-body chairs, technical leaders, and other stakeholders to shape substantive reviews, frame the questions that matter, and communicate conclusions clearly.
Translate feedback, recommendations, and decisions into concrete work with accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, and clear criteria for completion.
Drive that work forward across teams, resolve blockers, surface difficult tradeoffs, and escalate disagreements or resource gaps when needed.
Help teams understand which governance processes apply, integrate reviews into research and deployment plans, and identify changes that require further consideration.
Maintain clear records of decisions, rationale, conditions, commitments, exceptions, and unresolved questions.
Help improve governance practices, standards, and guidance as capabilities, evidence, and circumstances evolve.
Build and refine practical tools, operating cadences, and sources of truth that improve the quality and pace of the work.
Develop trusted relationships across Research, Safety Systems, Preparedness, Security, Legal, Product, leadership, and relevant external partners.

OpenAI’s Legal team helps advance our mission by tackling novel legal issues in AI. Our team brings together professionals across technology, privacy, intellectual property, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation. Our regulatory compliance work turns legal requirements into practical programs that support responsible AI development and deployment.

As a Legal Program Manager focused on regulatory compliance, you will build and manage cross-functional programs that translate counsel’s guidance into practical, sustainable operations. Your initial focus may include content moderation and/or frontier AI governance, with the mix shaped by team priorities and your strengths.
You will partner with internal and external counsel, other legal program managers, and technical and business teams to coordinate implementation, evidence collection, reporting, and ongoing compliance. You’ll build repeatable systems that scale across regulations, products, and jurisdictions, helping teams navigate emerging requirements with clarity and sound judgment.
This full-time role is based in San Francisco, CA, or New York, NY.

Lead regulatory compliance programs end to end: define scope, owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, and escalation paths, and drive execution with counsel and cross-functional partners.
Translate counsel’s regulatory guidance into repeatable workflows, controls, and documentation. Depending on your portfolio, this may include content moderation disclosures, transparency reporting, reporting and appeals workflows, or frontier AI model launch readiness, evaluation and risk-management evidence, and incident reporting.
Build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, User Operations, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), Global Affairs, Communications, and Go-to-Market to align program priorities and deliverables.
Support regulatory inquiries, audits and investigations with counsel, organizing evidence and responses to support timely, accurate communication and reporting.
Maintain a reliable source of truth for obligations, controls, decisions, evidence, and reporting. Demonstrate compliance readiness and control effectiveness, and improve program timeliness and evidence quality.
Identify execution risks and compliance gaps, track remediation, and escalate blockers. Establish clear success measures and operating cadences, keeping legal conclusions subject to counsel’s review.

s.h: You might thrive in this role if you

Have 6+ years of experience in program management, regulatory compliance, or related fields in a tech-forward or highly regulated environment, including relevant legal, regulatory, or compliance program experience.
Have experience working with an in-house legal team; regulatory matters experience and in-house technology experience are strongly preferred.
Have demonstrated experience building and scaling compliance programs, translating legal or regulatory requirements into operational workflows, and maintaining reliable documentation and evidence in partnership with counsel.
Take ownership of complex projects, set and achieve milestones, synthesize cross-functional input, and build trust across legal, technical, and business teams.
Bring strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Exercise sound judgment under pressure, adapt to changing priorities, and make progress through ambiguity.
Are resourceful and hands-on, with enthusiasm for AI technology and the ability to quickly learn unfamiliar technical concepts and navigate fast-moving technical environments.
Bring familiarity with content moderation, online safety, frontier AI governance, data governance, privacy, or emerging technology law as a plus. Depth in either content moderation or frontier AI governance is valuable; expertise in both is not required.
Bring data analysis or SQL skills, or relevant professional qualifications such as PMP, PMI-ACP, CPA, or CISSP, as a plus.

Unsere Mitarbeitenden aus rund 40 Berufen unterstützen und fördern die Wiedereingliederung straffällig gewordener Menschen und setzen sich wirksam und fortschrittlich für eine sichere und gerechte Gesellschaft ein.
Die Bewährungs- und Vollzugsdienste (BVD) sind eine von acht Hauptabteilungen von JuWe. Sie sind zuständig für die Regelung und Steuerung des Vollzugs von Freiheitsstrafen und gerichtlich angeordneten Massnahmen sowie für die Bewährungshilfe und die Durchführung von Lernprogrammen. Im Zentrum stehen die individuelle Begleitung sowie die Sicherstellung der Einhaltung von Auflagen in unterschiedlichen Massnahmensettings. Ein anspruchsvolles Umfeld, das neben fachlicher Kompetenz auch eine klare und erfahrene Führung verlangt.

1. Process Kaizen & SOP Governance

Nebius is an AI cloud company building a full-stack platform for developers and companies to take charge of their AI future, from data and model training through to production deployment. As European Affairs Projects Coordinator, you will support the planning and delivery of Nebius ' European affairs agenda.

You will manage the team's engagement calendar and project pipeline; coordinate partnerships, memberships and external contributions; and organise Nebius ' participation in conferences, roundtables, policy forums and stakeholder meetings across Europe.

Working closely with the European Affairs lead and internal teams, you will assess opportunities, prepare executives and subject-matter experts, coordinate content and logistics, track commitments and follow-up, and help strengthen Nebius' visibility and relationships across the European technology, policy and institutional ecosystem.

The role combines disciplined project management with hands-on external engagement support and is designed to develop over time: you should bring a foundational understanding of the Dutch and European policy and regulatory landscape, while Nebius will support you in deepening that knowledge and progressively applying the practical toolbox of Dutch and European affairs.

European affairs project coordination. Maintain the annual workplan and project pipeline, including priorities, owners, milestones, deadlines, budgets, dependencies and follow-up actions. Drive timely delivery across multiple concurrent workstreams and flag risks or decisions early.
Engagement calendar and executive scheduling. Own the European affairs calendar for external meetings, speaking engagements, conferences, delegations and partner activities. Triage invitations, coordinate availability and travel, and ensure senior participants are briefed and prepared.
Partnerships, memberships and external networks. Coordinate relationships with trade associations, technology and infrastructure partners, think tanks, academic and research organisations , chambers of commerce and relevant civil-society groups. Track memberships, working groups, renewals, commitments, opportunities and value delivered.
Events and external participation. Identify and assess relevant conferences, roundtables, workshops and policy forums. Manage registrations, sponsorship proposals, speaking submissions, speaker biographies, agendas, presentation materials, logistics and on-site support; help deliver Nebius -hosted events where required .
Contributions and briefing materials. Coordinate Nebius' contributions to panels, partner initiatives, publications, research projects and industry discussions. Prepare or consolidate briefing notes, talking points, event remarks, presentations, background materials and post-event summaries.
Internal alignment, monitoring and reporting. Coordinate closely with Communications, Marketing, Legal, Commercial, Partnerships, Infrastructure and leadership teams.

Maintain a practical overview of relevant Dutch and European institutional, policy, regulatory, industry and technology developments; keep accurate stakeholder and engagement records; capture actions, spend and outcomes; and provide concise updates on priorities, risks and opportunities.

Escalate substantive policy or legal questions to the appropriate owners .

At least three years of relevant experience : in European affairs, public affairs, stakeholder engagement, partnerships, events, programme or project coordination, ideally in a corporate, trade association, public institution or consultancy environment.
Strong project, calendar and event management : with a track record of coordinating multiple deadlines, participants, suppliers, travel and deliverables accurately.
Foundational understanding of the Dutch and European affairs ecosystem : including the policy and regulatory landscape, EU institutions, Dutch public authorities, trade associations, think tanks, industry forums and the ways companies engage with them.
Excellent written and verbal communication : with the ability to prepare clear briefings, event materials, correspondence and executive-ready updates in English.
Strong stakeholder management, discretion and attention to detail : comfortable working with senior leaders and a wide range of internal and external partners across countries and time zones, while using calendar, project- tracking and collaboration tools confidently.

Experience in technology, AI, cloud infrastructure, data centres , digital policy or another fast-moving B2B sector.
Experience coordinating trade-association memberships, strategic partnerships, sponsorships, speaker programmes or company-hosted events.
Familiarity with Brussels and the broader European technology and policy community.
Relevant bachelor's or master's degree; fluency in an additional European language is an advantage.

Manage client’s expectation effectively.
